represents: About an hour of det-eng-keyed syscalls on a developer/admin workstation (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8, GNOME on Wayland, Firefox snap, Docker Engine with runc 1.1): GPU/tty ioctls, shell pipelines, git/ssh/make/gcc/go/cargo/python/node/VS Code, systemd and snap-confine cgroup-BPF loads, resolved/NetworkManager/sshd/sudo/apt, memfd shared memory (Firefox, PipeWire, mutter, Xwayland), a docker-proxy splicing a local Postgres/Redis port, docker exec/run through runc; plus admin and debugging work adjacent to the rules: gdb/dlv/strace, perf and async-profiler, bpftool and bcc execsnoop, tcpdump, ping/tracepath/mtr, `ip xfrm` and strongSwan charon-nm, `ip netns add/exec`, `unshare -rn`, systemd PrivateNetwork units, `cryptsetup open` of a LUKS2 backup disk (AF_ALG + kernel keyring), `keyctl show`, fio with io_uring.
provenance: synthetic; event shape = detections/validate_detections.py normalize() output for SYSCALL records keyed det-eng; only syscalls in detections/audit/atomic.rules; argument encodings from the syscall ABIs (socket family/type/protocol incl. SOCK_CLOEXEC/NONBLOCK bits, setsockopt level/optname, ioctl request numbers from asm-generic/ioctls.h, sockios.h, dm-ioctl.h and drm.h, bpf(2) command numbers, ptrace(2) requests, unshare/setns CLONE_* flags, memfd_create MFD_* flags), and documented tool behaviour (iputils ping datagram ICMP, libpcap TPACKET setup, iproute2 netlink options, gdb/Go PTRACE_TRACEME in the forked inferior, strace PTRACE_SEIZE + GET_SYSCALL_INFO, Go's splice pipe pool (pipe2 O_CLOEXEC|O_NONBLOCK), runc 1.1's memfd re-exec and nsexec stage names, snap-confine's device-cgroup BPF and preserved mount namespace, cryptsetup LUKS2 AF_ALG keyslot decryption and logon key). Pointer arguments are random addresses in the right regions; pids are fixed for daemons and drawn per tool session. Events are drawn independently, so multi-syscall sequences (e.g. runc's memfd_create -> execveat in one pid) are NOT reproduced as sequences; correlation rules see only their base events here, except where one long-lived process (docker-proxy) issues both halves.
